subtopics: Why partial class strings may not be detected

learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of handling dynamic class names correctly.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on handling dynamic class names correctly and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: The reliability of handling dynamic class names correctly affects whether Tailwind detects candidate classes and generates the CSS you expect at build time.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Why partial class strings may not be detected; Using complete class names; Mapping application states to static utility strings; Handling class names passed through component properties; Supporting server-generated or externally stored class names. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to handling dynamic class names correctly, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Replace a partial interpolated utility string with a map of complete class names and verify both states.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to handling dynamic class names correctly.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to handling dynamic class names correctly.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: Complete class strings are present in source, allowing Tailwind to detect both variants.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying handling dynamic class names correctly without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Handling Dynamic Class Names Correctly is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
